chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both):

The Prophet (may God bless him and his family) prayed the funeral prayer over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, and said: Indeed, ninety thousand angels, including Gabriel, came to pray over him. So I said: O Gabriel, what did he do to deserve your prayer over him? He said: Because of his recitation of "Say: He is God, the One" (Surah al-Ikhlas) while standing, sitting, riding, walking, going, and coming.

key_terms.الملائكة: Angels - celestial beings created from light who worship God and carry out His commands
key_terms.جبرئيل: Gabriel (Jibril) - the archangel who brought revelation to the prophets
key_terms.صلاة: Prayer/funeral prayer - here referring to salat al-janaza (funeral prayer)
key_terms.قل هو الله أحد: Surah al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112) - a short chapter affirming the absolute oneness of God

ai.seo_question: Why did 90,000 angels pray over Sa'd ibn Mu'adh?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the extraordinary honor bestowed upon Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, a prominent companion of the Prophet, at his funeral prayer. The Prophet reported that 90,000 angels including Gabriel attended his funeral. When the Prophet asked Gabriel what made Sa'd deserve such an angelic turnout, Gabriel explained it was because Sa'd constantly recited Surah al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112) in every state and condition of his life. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was the chief of the Aws tribe in Medina who died from wounds suffered at the Battle of the Trench (5 AH), and his funeral was renowned in Islamic tradition.
